features.feature: Wave 4 integrates canonical acceptance topology/pre-review/rollout guidance into both Codex and Claude role assets without making prompt prose authority
Verifier-owned versioned rollout case/report model derives aggregates and rejects caller verdict/aggregate fields
Measured rollout uses a real reproducible comparable baseline/candidate high-assurance Story cohort rather than synthetic-only fixtures
Report receipt binds source case rows, project/threshold version, workspace hashes, cost, review rounds, waivers, adapter results and quorum provenance
Docs-only, legacy and ordinary single-outcome controls measure supported false blocks without fabricated runtime proof
Supported omission/forgery defects and topology-only C2 deletion bite through real consumers and restore clean control

Flat project rollout thresholds cover transcript/mutation taxonomy, supported adapter sufficiency, sample floor, omission detection, false blocks, degraded-host mislabeling, waivers and non-shrinking checks
Unknown, partial, unsupported or disagreeing adapters remain non-authoritative and fail promotion deterministically
Opt-in enforce mechanically consumes the exact current signed PASS rollout receipt at the real transition consumer
Enforcement additionally requires genuine current full 3 rounds x 2 independent supported hosts; degraded 3x1 is never authority
Missing, stale, tampered or failing report/quorum/threshold inputs fail closed with stable codes at the real gate consumer
Rollback to warn/observe changes only blocking policy and preserves reports, receipts, transitions, diagnostics and evidence history
Canonical Story 6 plan and CLI docs update only after executable cohort and enforcement/rollback evidence pass, with exact measured output and commands
Wave 3A selective per-Story/per-policy applicability remains explicitly unimplemented and excluded from flat Wave 4
features.excluded_by: Wave 3A is optional for flat project rollout and mandatory before any selective enforcement claim; B-4043 explicitly forbids selective applicability.

features.feature: No second writable acceptance matrix, caller-authored rollout verdict or prompt claim becomes gate evidence

openQuestions.q: What verifier-owned, predeclared eligibility and selection rule freezes baseline/candidate cohort membership so an operator cannot cherry-pick favorable real Stories, and does the minimum N=3 mean three matched pairs or at least three Stories in each arm?
openQuestions.evidence: CHK-002 says registered real case records and rejects caller verdict/aggregates, but does not make cohort membership/selection non-caller-writable; CHK-003 says only 'at least 3 comparable samples'.
openQuestions.resolution: The verifier freezes membership as every eligible comparable high-assurance Story/case in the declared evaluation window; caller selection and omissions are rejected. Minimum N means at least three matched baseline/candidate pairs, therefore at least three samples in each arm. This is now explicit in plan.md CHK-002/CHK-003 and bound into the signed report.

openQuestions.q: Which exact reviewer/coverage/verification-intent role assets are in Wave 4 scope, or should the plan stop promising implementer/reviewer guidance and explicitly limit integration to lattice-implementer?
openQuestions.evidence: plan.md promises mirrored implementer/reviewer prompts and the canonical touchpoint inventory names implementer, verification-intent, coverage, and reviewer modules, while CHK-001 files.modify lists only lattice-implementer.md for each host.
openQuestions.resolution: Wave 4 covers mirrored implementer, test-case-reviewer verification-intent compatibility, topology critic, and concept/quality/test-coverage/docs/delivery reviewer assets for both Codex and Claude. CHK-001 files.modify now enumerates every exact asset plus the registry contract.

openQuestions.q: Is Wave 4 promotion required to achieve zero false passes across every registered seeded defect class, not only 100% topology-omission detection, and where is that canonical threshold encoded?
openQuestions.evidence: Wave 4 exit and Success Metrics require false-pass thresholds, but CHK-003's explicit thresholds name omission detection and false blocks without a general seeded-defect false-pass threshold.
